result.message: Reviewed the submitted rad2deg_ Triton candidate (sha256 72f27523c6a7aa9ed34de7f122e86469ce65fb6abe065696520b0b923441cf24) in .best_kernel.py against the catalog Definition/oracle, the 24 correctness and 12 timing workloads, the four-round optimize ledger, and the review_tests/preflight receipts. The candidate is a genuine self-contained Triton implementation (masked contiguous kernel plus a rank<=8 strided-view kernel and a pre-bound launcher), preserves the declared mutates-A / returns-alias ABI, returns the mutated tensor, does not compute through torch.ops, does not special-case benchmark values beyond a general numel tile ladder, and contains no device synchronize or environment mutation. The oracle (oracle.py:71-76) calls torch.rad2deg_ and is independent of the candidate. Round 4 records 36/36 workloads passing (evaluate.json:9-17; geo_mean 1.1342) and the final verification is PASSED (optimize_definition_output.json:8-12; geo_mean 1.1634). The review_tests stage was an explicit orchestration skip (review.json:2-6), so this code review does not re-establish the test contract. Three advisory P1 findings remain: the round-4 input-dtype multiply degrades bf16 accuracy from ~1e-3 to ~7.6e-3 relative with no bf16 speed gain (the ledger itself says the bf16 half must be reverted); the _bind try/except fallback can double-apply the in-place transform if the private launcher APIs raise after the first launch; and the fast path depends on private torch_npu/Triton internals with a process-global device/stream captured once. No P0 defect and no missing evidence dependency was established, and I make no claim about runtime execution beyond the recorded results.
